history.period: Founded 1850 by Lama Sherab Gyatso (Sokpo Sherab Gyatso), Mongolian astrologer-monk, head until 1905; 15-ft Maitreya Buddha commissioned 1918 under second head Kyabje Domo Geshe Rinpoche Ngawang Kalsang (1909-1952)
history.summary: NON-HINDU: Ghoom Monastery (official name Yiga Choeling) is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery, NOT a Hindu temple - it needs a keep-or-drop decision for this project. Founded 1850 by the Mongolian astrologer-monk Lama Sherab Gyatso, it is one of the oldest and first Gelugpa ('Yellow Hat') Tibetan Buddhist monasteries in the Darjeeling region. Its centrepiece is the 15-ft gold-painted, jewel-encrusted statue of Maitreya Buddha (Gyalwa Shampa, the future Buddha), commissioned in 1918 under the second head Domo Geshe Rinpoche; two oil lamps burn before it around the clock. It houses rare handwritten Buddhist manuscripts (including the 108-volume Kangyur), Tibetan murals and thangkas, and gave refuge to high-ranking Tibetan monks fleeing the 1959 Chinese occupation. A file is written per the schema; the record stands only if the project scope extends to Buddhist sites. CSV TOWN FLAG: the monastery is at Ghoom (~7-8 km from Darjeeling town centre), not in Darjeeling town itself.

town_description: Ghoom is a small Himalayan town at about 7,400-8,000 ft on the road from Siliguri to Darjeeling, known as the home of India's highest railway station (the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway's Ghoom station) and several Buddhist monasteries. It sits near Tiger Hill, with Kanchenjunga views, and is about 7-8 km from the Darjeeling town centre.
tradition: Buddhism (Tibetan, Gelugpa/Yellow Hat sect) - NOT Hindu
